explanation: Simultaneous independent productive rates add. Isolate an unknown rate by subtracting the known component from the joint rate.

worked.action: A takes 12 days and B 18 days for the same job; use 36 work units.
worked.justification: This convenient common scale leaves the underlying fractions unchanged.

worked.action: A does 3 units/day; B does 2. Together their rate is 5 units/day.
worked.justification: Independent simultaneous productive rates add; durations do not.

worked.action: Time =36/5 =7.2 days. If a pair instead completes 1/6 job/day and A alone does 1/10, B does 1/6-1/10 =1/15 job/day.
worked.justification: The first problem divides work by combined rate; the second subtracts a known component from the combined rate.

worked.action: An outlet alone removes one full tank in 10 hours, while an inlet alone adds one tank in 15 hours. Take removal as positive.
worked.justification: Opposing flows change the same stored quantity in opposite directions.

worked.action: Net removal rate =1/10-1/15=1/30 tank/hour. Emptying an initially full tank takes30 hours.
worked.justification: Subtract the inflow, then divide the initial volume by the positive net removal rate. If net removal were zero or negative, this model would not empty the tank.

hint: Choose work units and label each rate with work/time before calculating.
shortcut: Use work = rate times active time; a convenient common work unit can avoid awkward fractions.
limitation: The rates must describe the same job, remain constant during each modelled interval, and not interfere.

entry.stem: A completes a job in 24 days and B in 12 days. At constant independent rates, how many days do they need together?
explanations: 36 adds durations, but simultaneous workers add work per day.
18 averages durations; it does not add rates.
The rate is 1/24 + 1/12 = 1/8 job per day, giving 8 days.
12 is B alone; A also contributes, so together they finish sooner.
repairs: Write work/day for each worker before adding.
Use equal work units, not an average of times.
Check that the joint time is below both solo times.
Include both productive rates.
reason_options: Add work per day, then divide one job by the sum
Add the two solo durations
entry.reason_explanation: Both workers produce parts of the same job during each shared day.
